column1: # DRAFT — Enterobacterales skani species-reference panel. David decides the panel; nothing here is a decision of record.
# Columns: species (the name the species call reports; a name may repeat: collate keeps the best ANI per name),
# NCBI assembly accession, the NCBI taxid the accession must descend from (species, or subspecies for subspecies
# rows), why the accession was chosen, strain. build_entero_genomes.sh reads columns 1-2 only.
# Chosen from the NCBI Datasets v2 REST API, never from memory (2026-11-20):
#   subspecies (NCBI designates reference genomes per species only), type strains:
# Verified per row (every row must print current, and "reference genome" or TYPE_MATERIAL; no TAXON line):
#   grep -v '^#' species_reference_panel.tsv | tail -n +2 | while IFS=$'\t' read -r sp acc taxid basis strain; do
# Not in the panel, for David to decide:
# - Klebsiella variicola subsp. tropica (KpSC phylogroup Kp5): NCBI has no reference genome and no type-material
#   assembly for it (taxon 2489014). A tropica genome will be called K. variicola, the reference below being subsp.
# - Klebsiella quasipneumoniae's species reference genome (GCF_020099175.1, FDAARGOS_1503) names no subspecies, so
#   the two subspecies' type strains stand in for it.
# - Escherichia coli phylogroups B1, B2 and D have no reference here (K-12 is phylogroup A, Sakai E). Shigella sits
#   inside E. coli at species-level ANI, so an E. coli genome may be called a Shigella: read the crosstab first.
# - The S. enterica subsp. indica type assembly carries 9.35 % CheckM contamination in its NCBI report.
# - Shigella boydii's reference genome is contig-level (ESBL-W3-2).
